It now also reads named budget constants. The four new budgets it surfaces are reported in a separate DISCLOSURE section and are deliberately NOT counted as suppressions: 10000ms (story-render precondition, sk-team-overview-shell-layout), 1500ms (font settle) and 5000ms (composition settle) in that file, and 5000ms (scroll settle default) in sk-workflow-board. criteria.notes: CORRECTED by the pre-merge squad, evidence lens. The previous entry closed this at a4facaa2 and was five commits stale across two commits that added wait durations, one of them a 20000ms literal disclosed nowhere. That literal has since been REPLACED with 10000ms so the helper's worst case stays well inside Playwright's default 30000ms per-test timeout, preserving the self-describing failure message instead of a bare 'Test timeout exceeded'. A new wait budget is classified as a DISCLOSURE rather than a suppression on purpose: counting one would make this criterion and C-001 unachievable for any mission that legitimately adds a precondition wait, which pressures the next author to avoid the rule rather than disclose under it. What the scan now guarantees is that new budgets are VISIBLE and individually accounted for here; before this repair, four were invisible.

It is now met on its own terms rather than reinterpreted. Root cause was Finding 4 (evidence/SHARED-CAUSE-INVESTIGATION.md): loadComposition injected over #storybook-root before Storybook's client-side render had run, so a render landing second destroyed the composition and the host was absent for the whole settle budget. Arm A went 74/80 -> 80/80 across that fix, which is what establishes the earlier contention sensitivity as a consequence of the render race rather than an independent cause.
